questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: What does P95 response time indicate?

options.A: 95% of requests completed within this duration
options.B: Average response time of all requests
options.C: Maximum response time observed
options.D: Minimum response time observed

questions.explanation: P95 means 95 percent of observed response times fall below this value, revealing tail performance that averages hide.

questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: Which test type deliberately pushes the system beyond normal operating limits?

options.A: Stress testing
options.B: Load testing
options.C: Soak testing
options.D: Smoke testing

questions.explanation: Stress testing deliberately exceeds normal capacity to find the breaking point and observe how the system degrades or recovers.

questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: What is throughput?

options.A: The rate at which work is completed, such as transactions per second
options.B: The duration of each individual transaction
options.C: The amount of memory consumed by the process
options.D: The number of users currently logged in

questions.explanation: Throughput measures how much work the system processes per unit of time, commonly transactions or requests per second.

questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: Which metric measures the time from sending a request to receiving the first byte of response?

options.A: Latency
options.B: Bandwidth
options.C: Throughput
options.D: Error rate

questions.explanation: Latency is the elapsed time between issuing a request and receiving the first byte of response, reflecting network plus server processing delay.

questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: What does a rising error rate during load testing typically indicate?

options.A: Resource exhaustion or instability under increasing load
options.B: The network cable is unplugged
options.C: The database is offline
options.D: All users have logged out

questions.explanation: A climbing error rate under load signals contention, queue saturation, or capacity limits that prevent requests from completing successfully.

questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: What is a check, in the context of performance metrics?

options.A: A programmatic verification of a response, such as correctness or status code
options.B: A rest break taken by the tester during execution
options.C: A financial payment made to the tool vendor
options.D: A manual note written on paper

questions.explanation: Checks verify response status, content, or timing during a performance test; their failure rate contributes to the overall error rate.

questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: What is the purpose of a spike test?

options.A: To evaluate behaviour under a sudden sharp increase in load followed by a return to baseline
options.B: To draw a spike shape on a performance chart
options.C: To test a single request in isolation
options.D: To reduce the number of virtual users gradually

questions.explanation: Spike testing rapidly injects a burst of load to check whether the system can absorb and recover from abrupt traffic surges.

questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: Which metric defines the proportion of requests that fail during a test run?

options.A: Error rate
options.B: Throughput
options.C: Latency
options.D: Think time

questions.explanation: Error rate expresses failed requests as a percentage of total requests and is a primary indicator of stability under load.

questions.domain: The Basic Concepts of Performance Testing
questions.question: What does concurrency measure in performance testing?

options.A: The number of users or requests being processed simultaneously
options.B: The total number of users who ever used the system
options.C: The physical number of servers in the data centre
options.D: The elapsed duration of the test run

questions.explanation: Concurrency is the count of virtual users or requests active at the same instant, which drives contention for shared resources.

questions.question: Why are percentiles preferred over averages when reporting performance?

options.A: They reveal the experience of slow requests that averages conceal
options.B: They are always easier to compute
options.C: They require no monitoring tooling
options.D: They make every result look better

questions.explanation: Averages are dragged down by fast requests and hide tail latency; percentiles such as p90 and p95 expose what slower users actually experience.

questions.question: What does a flat throughput curve accompanied by rising response time indicate?

options.A: The system has saturated and extra load only queues rather than completing work
options.B: The system is underutilised and needs more load
options.C: The monitoring tool has failed
options.D: The test should be terminated immediately

questions.explanation: When throughput plateaus while response time keeps climbing, the system has passed its knee point and additional load produces queueing, not useful work.

questions.question: Why should a baseline be captured under stable, repeatable conditions?

options.A: So later results can be compared meaningfully against a known reference
options.B: So the test completes faster
options.C: So monitoring can be disabled
options.D: So the environment can be changed freely afterwards

questions.explanation: A baseline is only useful as a comparison point if it was captured under documented, reproducible conditions; otherwise differences cannot be attributed to the change under test.

questions.question: What is think time?

options.A: The simulated pause between user actions in a virtual user script
options.B: The time a tester spends planning the test
options.C: The time the tool spends compiling scripts
options.D: The delay before the test starts running

questions.explanation: Think time models realistic human pacing between actions so the generated load resembles genuine user traffic rather than machine-speed hammering.

questions.question: Which resource is most likely saturated if application CPU is low but response time is high?

options.A: A downstream dependency such as a database or external service
options.B: The application CPU itself
options.C: The test generator CPU
options.D: The monitor display refresh rate

questions.explanation: When the application's own CPU is idle yet latency is high, time is being spent waiting on a dependency such as a database, cache, or third-party API.

questions.question: Why run a performance test more than once before drawing conclusions?

options.A: Run-to-run variance can make a single measurement misleading
options.B: The tool requires multiple runs to license correctly
options.C: Results are always identical between runs
options.D: Multiple runs are needed to exceed a minimum test duration

questions.explanation: Aggregating several runs reduces the influence of transient noise such as cold caches, background jobs, or network jitter, giving a more trustworthy picture.

questions.question: What does a saturated connection pool typically cause?

options.A: Requests queue and eventually time out waiting for a free connection
options.B: Faster response times because connections are reused
options.C: Lower memory usage across the application
options.D: Improved throughput with no side effects

questions.explanation: Once all pooled connections are in use, further requests must wait; queueing grows until waiters exceed timeout thresholds and fail.

questions.question: Why monitor both server-side and client-side timing?

options.A: Server processing time alone does not reflect the latency users actually experience
options.B: Client-side timing is always inaccurate
options.C: Server-side timing includes rendering automatically
options.D: Both metrics are identical in every system

questions.explanation: Network transfer, TLS negotiation, and browser rendering add to what the user perceives, so end-to-end timing is needed alongside server metrics.

questions.domain: Performance Testing in the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Why is shifting performance testing earlier in the lifecycle beneficial?

options.A: Defects found early are cheaper and easier to correct than those found after release
options.B: Performance testing is only meaningful before any code exists
options.C: Early testing removes the need for later performance tests
options.D: Early tests require no environment setup

questions.explanation: Architectural and algorithmic performance problems are far cheaper to fix before release, when changes are local rather than cross-cutting.

questions.domain: Performance Testing in the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: What is the main risk of testing only against a scaled-down environment?

options.A: Bottlenecks that appear only at production scale may remain undiscovered
options.B: Scaled-down environments are always more accurate
options.C: Smaller environments cannot run any performance tests
options.D: Production environments never reveal new bottlenecks

questions.explanation: Data volume, concurrency, and topology differences mean small environments can hide bottlenecks that only emerge at full scale.

questions.domain: Performance Testing in the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: How does performance testing fit into a CI/CD pipeline?

options.A: A lightweight automated subset gates merges while heavier suites run periodically
options.B: All performance tests must run synchronously on every commit
options.C: Performance testing cannot be automated in CI/CD
options.D: Performance testing replaces functional testing in the pipeline

questions.explanation: A fast smoke-level performance check can gate merges, while longer soak and stress suites run on a schedule to avoid blocking the pipeline.

questions.domain: Performance Testing in the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Why include performance acceptance criteria in a release gate?

options.A: To make release decisions objective rather than based on opinion
options.B: To make releases slower for no benefit
options.C: To avoid the need for any monitoring
options.D: To remove the need for stakeholders

questions.explanation: Explicit thresholds such as p95 under 500 ms or error rate below 1 percent convert performance into a pass or fail gate instead of a subjective judgement.

questions.domain: Performance Testing in the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: What is the value of a canary release for performance validation?

options.A: A small slice of real traffic exposes the new version to production conditions before full rollout
options.B: It removes the need for load testing entirely
options.C: It guarantees no performance regressions
options.D: It replaces the staging environment

questions.explanation: Routing a fraction of live traffic to the new version surfaces real-world performance behaviour with limited blast radius before a full switch.

questions.question: What is a workload model?

options.A: A representation of the user types, transaction mix, and arrival pattern the test will simulate
options.B: A diagram of the physical data centre layout
options.C: A list of the developers assigned to the project
options.D: A schedule of meetings during the test phase

questions.explanation: The workload model defines who uses the system, what they do, and how often they arrive, forming the basis for realistic load generation.

questions.question: Why parameterise test data across virtual users?

options.A: Identical data causes unrealistic cache hits and hides real query costs
options.B: Parameterisation is only needed for functional tests
options.C: It reduces the number of virtual users required
options.D: It removes the need for a database

questions.explanation: When every user submits the same values, caches and indexes serve them trivially, understating the cost of realistic varied requests.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a ramp-up phase?

options.A: To increase load gradually so warm-up effects and the point of degradation are observable
options.B: To waste the first portion of the test
options.C: To reduce the peak concurrency achieved
options.D: To avoid collecting metrics during warm-up

questions.explanation: A gradual ramp lets caches warm and threads start up, while revealing the knee point at which response time begins to rise sharply.

questions.question: Why define exit criteria before running a performance test?

options.A: To agree in advance what result counts as acceptable, avoiding post-hoc debate
options.B: To guarantee the test will pass
options.C: To reduce the number of metrics collected
options.D: To avoid the need for a baseline

questions.explanation: Pre-agreed exit criteria such as throughput and error-rate thresholds make the outcome objective and prevent arguments after results are known.

questions.question: What should be done when a test run produces suspiciously good results?

options.A: Verify the load generators were not saturated and that requests actually reached the target
options.B: Immediately publish the results as a success
options.C: Disable monitoring to avoid further confusion
options.D: Reduce the load and rerun

questions.explanation: Implausibly good results commonly mean the generators bottlenecked or requests failed before reaching the application, so validity must be confirmed first.

questions.question: Why correlate application logs and infrastructure metrics during a run?

options.A: The combination distinguishes application-level from infrastructure-level causes of slowness
options.B: Logs are only useful for functional defects
options.C: Metrics are only useful after the test ends
options.D: Correlation doubles the volume of data with no benefit

questions.explanation: Joining application traces with host metrics shows whether a slow span is caused by application code, CPU, memory pressure, disk I/O, or the network.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a soak test?

options.A: To reveal resource leaks and gradual degradation over an extended run
options.B: To find the maximum instantaneous load
options.C: To measure single-request latency
options.D: To validate user interface rendering

questions.explanation: Running steady load for hours exposes slowly growing memory or handle usage, connection leaks, and gradual throughput decay that short tests miss.

questions.question: Why confirm the test environment matches production topology?

options.A: Different topology changes where bottlenecks occur and invalidates comparisons
options.B: Topology only affects security, not performance
options.C: A simpler topology always produces equivalent results
options.D: Topology only matters for functional testing

questions.explanation: Load balancers, instance counts, and network hops determine where contention appears, so topology differences can move or mask bottlenecks entirely.

questions.question: Which activity should precede test design in a performance testing project?

options.A: Defining performance requirements and acceptance criteria
options.B: Selecting the colour scheme for reports
options.C: Purchasing additional hardware
options.D: Writing the final report

questions.explanation: Clear, measurable performance requirements must exist before test design, otherwise there is no basis for choosing workloads or deciding pass or fail.

questions.question: What is the primary task of the performance tester during test execution?

options.A: Monitoring the run and the system, capturing evidence, and deciding whether the data is valid
options.B: Writing new features for the system under test
options.C: Configuring the production database
options.D: Approving the release

questions.explanation: During execution the tester watches for generator saturation, unexpected errors, and system anomalies, and judges whether the collected data can be trusted.

questions.question: Why record the environment configuration alongside results?

options.A: Results are only interpretable when the environment that produced them is known
options.B: Configuration details are only needed for audit
options.C: It has no bearing on interpreting results
options.D: It is required only for cloud deployments

questions.explanation: Hardware, versions, data volume, and topology materially affect results, so without recording them a result cannot be reproduced or compared.

questions.question: What distinguishes a performance defect from a functional defect?

options.A: A performance defect concerns speed, capacity, or resource use rather than incorrect behaviour
options.B: Performance defects are always less important
options.C: Functional defects never affect performance
options.D: Performance defects cannot be reported in the same tracker

questions.explanation: Performance defects describe unacceptable latency, throughput, or resource consumption under specified conditions rather than wrong outputs.

questions.question: Why involve stakeholders when interpreting performance results?

options.A: Thresholds for acceptable performance depend on business context and user expectations
options.B: Stakeholders are only needed to approve the budget
options.C: Performance results are self-explanatory
options.D: Stakeholders should be kept away from technical data

questions.explanation: Whether a given p95 is acceptable depends on user expectations and business criticality, which stakeholders are best placed to define.

questions.question: What is a load generator in a performance testing tool?

options.A: The component that creates virtual user traffic against the system under test
options.B: The component that stores test results
options.C: The component that generates reports
options.D: The component that provisions servers

questions.explanation: The load generator drives the simulated traffic; if it saturates before the target system does, the results are invalid.

questions.question: Why distribute load generation across multiple machines?

options.A: A single generator may saturate before the system under test reaches its limit
options.B: Distribution always improves result accuracy
options.C: It removes the need for think time
options.D: It eliminates the need for monitoring

questions.explanation: One machine has finite CPU, memory, and network capacity; when the target can absorb more load than the generator can produce, additional generators are required.

questions.question: What is the benefit of recording and replaying real production traffic?

options.A: It produces a workload closely matching genuine usage patterns
options.B: It removes the need for any test data
options.C: It guarantees the absence of bottlenecks
options.D: It eliminates the need for a test environment

questions.explanation: Replaying captured traffic produces a workload distribution grounded in reality, including the awkward request mixes that synthetic scripts often omit.

questions.question: Why should performance test scripts be version controlled?

options.A: To reproduce the exact scenarios behind historical results and review changes over time
options.B: Because scripting tools require it to run
options.C: To reduce the size of the repository
options.D: Because scripts never change once written

questions.explanation: Version control allows a past result to be tied to the precise script that produced it, enabling meaningful comparison when results change.

questions.question: What capability matters most when choosing a tool for protocol-level testing?

options.A: Support for the protocols and message formats used by the system under test
options.B: The visual appeal of its dashboard
options.C: The number of bundled sample tests
options.D: The size of its installation package

questions.explanation: If the tool cannot speak the required protocols, no amount of reporting or scripting convenience will make the test possible.

questions.question: Why is analysing the tool's own resource usage important?

options.A: A saturated tool produces misleading results about the system under test
options.B: Tool usage never affects results
options.C: It only matters for very small tests
options.D: It is purely a licensing consideration

questions.explanation: If the generator or its host saturates, throughput and latency figures reflect the tool's limits rather than the target system's behaviour.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a correlation step when scripting against a dynamic application?

options.A: To capture values produced by the server and reuse them in later requests
options.B: To correlate the test results with the project budget
options.C: To align the tool with the team's calendar
options.D: To match test data across environments

questions.explanation: Session identifiers, tokens, and anti-CSRF values are generated per session; extracting them dynamically lets a virtual user chain requests successfully.

questions.question: Why is a lightweight performance smoke test useful in a pipeline?

options.A: It catches gross regressions quickly without the cost of a full load test
options.B: It replaces the need for any load testing
options.C: It provides statistically rigorous capacity figures
options.D: It removes the need for monitoring in production

questions.explanation: A short, low-concurrency check can flag major regressions on every build while deeper capacity testing runs less frequently.

questions.question: What should be verified before trusting results from a new test script?

options.A: That it executes the intended user journey and its checks pass at low concurrency
options.B: That it compiles without syntax errors only
options.C: That it produces a large result file
options.D: That it runs for at least one hour

questions.explanation: A script must be validated functionally at single-user concurrency before being used for load, otherwise it may be exercising the wrong path or failing silently.

questions.question: Why keep separate load generator machines on the same network segment as the target?

options.A: Network distance and bandwidth can dominate measured latency and distort results
options.B: It guarantees identical results across environments
options.C: It removes the need for think time
options.D: It reduces licensing costs

questions.explanation: If generators sit far from the target or share saturated links, measured latency includes network effects that production users may not experience.
